replacements.from: This server has no URL scraper, OCR, or document/image parser of its own — extracting the recipe's content from whatever source the user gives you (reading the page, reading the image, reading the document, or just using the pasted/described text) is your job, using your own capabilities. The tools below only persist what you've already extracted.
replacements.to: Native import tools delegate URL scraping, HTML/schema.org JSON parsing and ZIP import to Mealie: use import_recipe_from_url, import_recipe_from_html_or_json or import_recipe_from_zip when requested. They create recipes and may import taxonomy according to their flags. After an ambiguous write, inspect before repeating. This server adds no OCR or document/image parser. For manual creation from text, images or documents, extract content using your own capabilities and follow the workflow below.

replacements.from: 2. **Fill in scalar metadata with `patch_recipe`.** Set `description` and `recipeYield` from the source when available. Mealie only exposes one aggregate time field here (`totalTime`) — there's no separate prep/cook time to populate. Prefer the source's own explicit total time when it states one. If the source only gives component times (prep, cook, rest, chill, marinate, proof, etc.), derive a single `totalTime` only when the source makes their relationship clear enough to do so faithfully — don't blindly sum prep + cook, since real total time often isn't just their sum (overlapping work, resting/chilling/marinating/proofing time, etc.). Otherwise leave `totalTime` unset rather than guessing.
replacements.to: 2. **Fill in metadata.** Legacy patch_recipe retains its original arguments. Use update_recipe_metadata with the latest expectedUpdatedAt to edit description, orgURL, servings/yield, totalTime, prepTime, cookTime, performTime, nutrition, settings and extras. Nested objects merge with current state, preserving omitted fields; nutrition:null clears the block. Copy times and nutrition from the source, never invent them or blindly sum overlapping component times. Change privacy or locking only when explicitly requested.

replacements.from: 6. **Preserve the source URL when the available recipe schema supports it.** The current toolset does not expose Mealie's source-URL field, so don't invent one, and don't default to stuffing the URL into `description` just to work around the gap. If the user explicitly wants provenance retained despite this limitation, using `description` as a fallback is acceptable — but treat that as an explicit workaround, not the default behavior.
replacements.to: 6. **Preserve the source URL in orgURL**, using patch_recipe or update_recipe_metadata. Do not put it into description as a workaround when the dedicated field is available.

append:
## Additional Recipe Operations

get_recipe_notes reads notes and a fresh updatedAt. add_recipe_note appends; update_recipe_note edits title/text by stable referenceId; delete_recipe_note deletes that identity. All writes require expectedUpdatedAt. Recipe notes differ from ingredient note fields and user comments. Deleting a linked note requires explicit removeReferences:true. On stale snapshots, re-read and reassess without automatic replay.

Use get_recipe_comments/create_recipe_comment/update_recipe_comment/delete_recipe_comment for user comments; Mealie enforces ownership. get_recipe_share_links/create_recipe_share_link/delete_recipe_share_link manage shared access: create or reveal tokens only for an explicit sharing request, never as a cleanup side effect. Timeline tools list/create/update/delete events and upload event images; the provider controls editability.

upload_recipe_asset and create_recipe_asset_from_url add attachments, available in get_recipe_detailed. get_recipe_export_formats discovers formats; export_recipe returns bounded dataBase64, filename and mediaType without writing host files. Native imports are additional options alongside manual creation. Never log recipe/file contents, credentials or signed URLs.
